# Typed document application

`createDocumentApplication` in `index.mjs` is an inert Fetch boundary. It returns `{handle(Request)}` and owns no pool, session registry, listener, executor, storage or shutdown operation. The caller retains those resources. `enabled` defaults to `false`; this does not alter the canonical catalog's null handlers or runtime qualification.

```js
const app = createDocumentApplication({
  sessions: {authenticateSession, readCurrentState},
  selectedClientId, artifactOptions, credential, now,
  limits: {maxRequestMs: 15000, maxRequestBytes: 131072, maxResponseBytes: 1048576},
  enabled: true,
});
```

`artifactOptions` is the existing `createPostgresArtifactService` configuration, with the canonical `artifactValidators` object, the **same** `now` function, and the exact `create_word` catalog descriptor projection `{operation,requiredGrants,sourceRequirements}`. Its prebound context, producer identity, immutable allocation and original expiry remain unchanged between deliveries. The caller performs canonical grant binding separately. The configured `credential` is the trusted artifact capability; it is never obtained from the HTTP request. The HTTP Bearer is a separately issued opaque action session. Existing `/api/action-followthrough/session` issuance can be mounted alongside this app on the same trusted host, as shown by the root-owned `local/mount.mjs`. No browser-provided identity, grant, scope, asset or evidence is admitted.

All four routes are POST with JSON and `Authorization: Bearer <opaque session>`:

| Route | Exact body | Success |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/api/documents/create` | `{deliveryId,request}` | `{version,inspection,execution}` |
| `/api/documents/revise` | `{deliveryId,baseVersionId,request}` | `{version,inspection,execution}` |
| `/api/documents/inspect` | `{versionId}` | `{version,inspection}` |
| `/api/documents/download` | `{versionId}` | Exact verified bytes with attachment filename and MIME |

`request` is the canonical typed `WordRequest` with `operation:'create_word'` and `format:'docx'` or `'txt'`. For DOCX, text uses blocks such as `{kind:'paragraph',runs:[{text:'Draft text'}]}`. TXT uses `{content:{text:'Draft text'}}`. Titles, tables, runs and supported chart/image references follow existing artifact contracts. PDF is intentionally not admitted by this application. No natural-language model loop, approval choice or new renderer is introduced. Revision is a new full typed replacement based on the exact immutable prior version; it is not an in-place patch. Existing service verification preserves the original bytes and parent relationship.

A session fresh check precedes execution, every configured artifact/capability authorization boundary, and release. Current full binding, ordered scopes and selected client must equal the configured context. All session/authority cutoffs shorten one request lifetime; the original artifact context is not rewritten, so repeat delivery identity is stable. Older versions are read under current authority without changing their original version provenance. Reads use the existing artifact service and cannot call the canonical budget reservation/settlement path.

Responses have `Cache-Control: no-store` and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`; no CORS permission is added. Downloads retain the canonical ASCII filename and MIME, and verify length/hash again before release. Borrowed port rejections are converted to inert content-free errors before passing into canonical owners; Proxy and accessor properties are not evaluated. Errors contain only `{error:{code,outcome}}`, never provider messages, credentials or draft content. Malformed route/body/media is refused before effects; session denial is 403, disabled application 503, timeout 408, cancellation 499, and other owner failures 502. Shared body size failures retain 413. A started write with uncertain completion is `UNKNOWN`; a returned result rejected at release is `RESULT_NOT_RELEASED`; unsuccessful reads are `READ_UNAVAILABLE`. These are conservative dispositions, not rollback or physical-cancellation proofs.

The same delivery is not regenerated. This boundary performs no automatic retry, refund, recovery mutation or fresh delivery allocation. Canonical historical reconciliation remains the artifact PostgreSQL owner's responsibility. Local structural inspection and actual DOCX bytes do not establish native Office rendering, visual quality, production identity, physical sandbox isolation or real database qualification.

# Document application source outline

The Fetch boundary admits fixed typed create_word docx/txt requests. It does not interpret prose, create authority, generate approvals, or implement rendering. Existing session issuance remains independently mounted. HTTP bearer credentials are opaque sessions; the configured artifact capability never comes from the body.

`createDocumentApplication({sessions,selectedClientId,artifactOptions,credential,now,limits,enabled=false})` returns `{handle}`. Limits are maxRequestMs/maxRequestBytes/maxResponseBytes. The original canonical artifact context is snapshotted once; its deadline, evidence, assets, scopes and binding are never rewritten to produce a different delivery hash.

Modules: http.mjs owns native Request admission and content-free responses; current.mjs composes createRequestCurrent and captures trusted configuration; index.mjs dispatches to actual artifact owners and validates release. Canonical artifact validators and format helpers own shapes/filenames. PostgresArtifactService owns all write accounting and replay; ArtifactService owns read verification without budget reservation. Every authority boundary and final release rechecks current sessions and exact configured binding/scopes/client. Session and authority expiries synchronously narrow one outer lifetime before another port can run.

Routes: POST /api/documents/create {deliveryId,request}; revise {deliveryId,baseVersionId,request}; inspect/download {versionId}. JSON results are existing artifact results. Download returns exact verified bytes with attachment MIME/filename. Errors contain only a finite code and disposition; write calls with uncertain completion remain UNKNOWN, and acknowledged output denied at release remains RESULT_NOT_RELEASED. There is no automatic retry, reconciliation mutation, resource disposal, or production catalog activation.

Tests use actual canonical artifact services and budget ledger with explicitly scripted ports. Root separately owns actual local docx generation/HTTP flow. Test bounds are 180 seconds. No native database, provider, network service, or customer data is used by this author lane.

# Executable Word drafting fixture

Run from the repository root with its existing Node dependencies and the approved local Python libraries (`python-docx 1.2.0`, Pillow). The Python executable must be an absolute path:

```sh
node scripts/local-document/run.mjs --help
node scripts/local-document/run.mjs --run --python /opt/codex/runtimes/codex-primary-runtime/dependencies/python/bin/python
node --test apps/control/document-application/local/local.test.mjs
```

The command sets and restores its own source-root binding, allocates a private temporary directory and a loopback listener, obtains an opaque session through the existing issuance endpoint, and runs the real document application. It creates a DOCX brief, revises the paragraph and table, reconstructs the application graph, then inspects and downloads both exact versions. It reopens each downloaded package using python-docx and verifies the original text/table survived. Replaying the original write cannot regenerate it. Revoking the synthetic identity denies both historical downloads and a new write.

The PostgreSQL budget implementation runs against the existing scripted SQL test pool. Both versions use one bound grant and allocation and settle two synthetic 10 microUSD reservations. This is local accounting evidence; no paid model or database server is called. The existing local artifact store persists immutable objects and versions for the duration of the fixture. Reconstructing the application does not create new storage or reset the allocation.

The resulting JSON contains version/hash/lineage evidence, content inspection, accounting totals and child-process cleanup receipts. The command closes the listener and removes only its owned temporary files. A successful result requires closed process groups, no executor directories left behind, no open sockets and completed cleanup. The original 25-second fixture cutoff covers all requests. Help and malformed usage allocate no fixture, listener or subprocess.

Identity, source authorization and SQL are explicitly synthetic. The generated DOCX bytes, local immutable storage, HTTP transport and Python subprocesses are real. `nativeQualified:false`, `previewStatus:'pending'` and `generationStatus:'draft'` remain explicit. This does not qualify live Clerk, native PostgreSQL, Office rendering, visual quality, runtime sandboxing, production storage, SDK natural-language drafting or source filing. The registered production catalog remains disabled and preserves all selected capabilities; this fixture exercises only the Word drafting application increment.

`ports.mjs` and `fixture.mjs` are test-only. Product entry points must not import them. They intentionally create synthetic facts and must never be used as production authorization.

This is generic local drafting. Native meeting/memo source mutations remain deferred and filing remains a separate approved command.

Discovery found existing artifact generation, lineage, resource authorization, immutable storage and shared-budget owners with no non-test application/controller caller. The change wires them instead of adding a generator, identity system, persistence subsystem or registry. Ordinary ToolDispatch does not accept the artifact-execution profile; the existing dedicated PostgreSQL artifact owner is the correct write path. Its catalog output assertion models creation only; the application correlates revision results against the explicit parent and existing version schema.

- Existing artifacts/service.mjs: immutable versions, original bytes, resource authorization, inspection, downloads and uncertain-effect reporting.
- Existing artifacts/postgres-service.mjs and gateway budget owner: writes charged to the existing run allocation, durable delivery identity, settlement and replay refusal. No new accounting algorithm.
- Existing local executor and python-docx: real DOCX generation for the disposable source fixture. Existing local store retains objects and versions. Production storage remains separately supplied.
- Existing session issuance and Node HTTP listener: reused unchanged. Frontend and Capiro files are outside this lane.

No existing migration, public 0.1 contract, private artifact 0.2 schema, capability selection or production catalog handler changes. Production source connectivity remains disabled. An explicitly configured fixture can execute the new application.

# Meri shared contracts 0.1.0

Public distribution candidate for D014: `@capiro/meri-contracts` exports generated UI-event types at the package root, browser validation at `/browser`, immutable schema metadata at `/metadata`, the exact frozen JSON at `/schema`, and existing Node checks at `/node`. The package version does not change the frozen wire protocol. R2 additive candidates are intentionally absent from these exports until separately reviewed/frozen.

Run `npm ci --ignore-scripts --prefix packages/contracts`, then `npm run check:contracts:distribution`. Regenerate only with `npm run build --prefix packages/contracts`; `generate.mjs --check` compares deterministic generated bytes without writing. The generator refuses any drift from the accepted 50043-byte schema hash. Pack with `npm pack ./packages/contracts --ignore-scripts` at the repository root; consumers use the resulting versioned public tarball, never private source imports. Generated types describe shape and cannot express every format/bound; runtime validation remains required. Validation grants no authorization.

Owner: Codex integration. Status: prepared for independent review; freeze requires review acceptance and a pinned integration commit. `meri.schema.json` uses JSON Schema 2020-12, stable ID `urn:meri:contracts:0.1.0`, closed records, UTC timestamps, safe integers and explicit protocol versions. These independent definitions import no Capiro implementation. Subordinate tool argument/result schemas must be approved with each new connector; the generic `arguments` and `data` envelopes are deliberately opaque and are never permission grants.

`npm ci` followed by `npm run check:contracts` validates the contract boundary fixtures. Ajv handles shapes, formats and unknown fields. `canonicalize` supplies the RFC 8785 JSON encoding for SHA-256 over the complete `Command`, including its identity binding, operation, arguments, immutable attachments, lineage and idempotency key. Approval metadata and decisions are excluded from that preimage. A changed command always requires a new proposal and approval. Strict schemas mean added fields can break old readers; bump the contract version and qualify an adapter before dependent work.

## Required service semantics

- Resolve identity with the official Clerk backend SDK, then current authoritative local user and active tenant membership. Capability claims are server-verified metadata, never model-supplied authority. Validate signature/opaque grant lookup, issuer, audience, expiry, actions, actor, tenant, conversation, run, attempt, worker, budgets, current policy revision and writer fence at the trusted gateway/broker. No bearer keys belong in events, files, checkpoints or logs.
- Enforce all client walls, mailbox ownership and private-memory grants independently of tenant identity. Check current access to every protected contributing scope for tool reads, resume, publication, event replay, thread history, citations, previews, downloads and exports. Losing authority cancels affected live work and blocks historical content. A scope list alone proves no access.
- Every derived object inherits the union of contributing source scopes. Reject mismatched tenant bindings and dropped lineage. A public source does not erase private lineage. Citation IDs resolve through the gateway after authorization, rather than exposing raw storage URLs.
- Sequence events once per conversation in durable application storage. Immutable event IDs deduplicate delivery; reconnect requests events after an acknowledged sequence. Enforce ordering across runs/attempts and fence stale writers. UI events are separate from opaque SDK transcripts and do not expose private model reasoning.
- Bind opaque pagination cursors to the actor, current authorization revision, scopes, source, normalized query and continuation. Do not interpret a bounded empty scan as complete coverage. Truncated results cannot claim complete coverage; unsupported history and counts remain explicit.
- Execute approved commands only after current authorization, matching proposal/hash/approver/expiry and live fence checks. Atomically bind the tenant-scoped idempotency key to the exact command hash and outcome. Same key with a different hash conflicts. Reconcile indeterminate external outcomes before retrying; an SDK/Temporal retry alone cannot guarantee no duplicate side effects.
- `Command.binding` is immutable producer provenance. `CommandExecutionRequest.executorBinding` and capability identify the current trusted executor; compare stable tenant/actor/conversation/run identity with the approved intent, then authorize the current attempt/worker/fence independently. Approval-wait recovery may replace the executor without modifying approved intent or its idempotency identity. Source receipts bind the actual executor.
- A checkpoint requires independently verified durable SDK state AND workspace bytes/manifest, exact runtime/image/contract/skill versions, a trusted durable receipt and fencing. `durableReceiptId` in untrusted JSON does not prove durability. Verify all bytes/hashes/object permissions and compatibility before resume; unsupported links and traversal are rejected. Detect filesystem ancestor/descendant conflicts during restoration. Uploaded `.claude`, instructions, plugins and config remain inert data outside runtime discovery.
- Lifecycle tombstones and restore barriers must survive backup restoration. Apply deletion/retention to transcripts, events, uploads, browser state, snapshots, previews, artifacts, caches and exports. Legal holds need explicit policy; do not silently resurrect deleted material.
- Record measured usage for every run/attempt including failures, retries, cancellation and SDK subagents. Reconcile provider records and enforce budgets outside the agent. Temporal owns orchestration/schedules; nondeterministic execution belongs in activities or broker workers.

## Initial evidence boundary

The fixtures prove only local structural and immutable-payload/path checks. They do not prove authentication, current authorization, durable storage, cursor security, deletion, idempotent external execution, network isolation, browser sandboxing or Fargate compatibility. Those remain W02–W09 deployment evidence.

The revocation deadline is proposed at no more than 30 seconds and must be agreed before G3. Per-task and tenant cost caps must be chosen from qualification measurements. Production source reads/writes, schedules and authenticated browsing are disabled until their gates pass.

## Additive action application receiver (package 0.1.1)

`@capiro/meri-contracts/action-application` exports async `receiveActionResponse(route, httpStatus, jsonText)` and `ActionResponseError`, plus route-specific receiving TypeScript types. Use `await receiveActionResponse('query', response.status, await response.text())`. The input must be primitive JSON text: arbitrary objects, accessors and Proxies are rejected without inspection. A successful return is a detached, deeply frozen actual wire value (success or `{error:{code,outcome}}`). Only HTTP200 carries success. Other statuses must match the canonical content-free error code; errors throw content-free `ActionResponseError` codes. No endpoint, credential, approval or retry capability is exported.

The receiver requires browser WebCrypto SHA-256 and TextEncoder. It bounds UTF-8 text to16MiB, nesting to64 and parsed nodes to100,000; these last two are deliberate receiving limits. Nested contracts are generated from their canonical owners, including original public0.1 UIEvent/RunBinding/ApprovalProposal/CommandReceipt and the selected private read/task result definitions. Only the receiving projection is published: importing does not import any private server source. The new `/action-application/schema` export contains that projection; source hashes are in `dist/action-application.metadata.json`. Existing public0.1 schema and root/browser generated bytes are unchanged.

Hash equality and internal correlations do not authenticate source truth, transport or current access. Prepared means `approval_required`, never approved. An observed receipt is not a fresh grant or safe retry instruction. Execute responses omit the original proposal, so consumers must retain and separately correlate the trusted originating proposal/command when needed; this receiver cannot infer that missing fact. Recovered current attempts may differ from draft source provenance while stable tenant/actor/conversation/run identities remain correlated. UNKNOWN/RESULT_NOT_RELEASED/STORED_NOT_RELEASED/NOT_STORED/READ_UNAVAILABLE never imply rollback or retry permission.

Build/check includes `generate-actions.mjs`; it reads schemas and application error vocabulary at build time only. No runtime/API/model/provider/database activity occurs. Isolated installation uses the package tarball; no npm publication is authorized.
